title: slate-compiles-from-the-world
intention: The slate is compiled from instruments and written through a door: /saveslate reads the world first (git heads, ticket cursors touched, the standing chain), and the write-side gate refuses a slate whose packet's git heads do not match the LIVE repos (the writer never looked), carries keys nothing reads, or exceeds the standing-context ceiling — and the door itself writes the slate file, so there is no second path to CairnCommons/slates/.
why: Rank 5 of notes/2026-08-02-opus-compatibility-pass.json, ruled spec: the slate is injected into EVERY future session by the SessionStart hook — authoritative by construction — yet it is synthesized from the transcript with no instrument prescribed: the model that has already lost track of details writes a confident slate, and the next session inherits the loss as ground truth. Blast radius: every session, forever. Akien named /saveslate (with /sorted) as exactly what he had been feeling.
traces_to: Law 3 — the slate is a claim about the session; the instruments make it measured
Law 4/6 — one gated write path to the artifact every session inherits

proves_green.prove_gate: derivation gate — cairn cairnmap --gate green (the charter changes)
proves_green.proof_gate: proof teeth beside the code, injected roots, sealed netns, validation beside the code
proves_green.entry_gate: BUILDME rides the chart chain + intent berth + sorted berth
proves_green.durability_gate: not done until proven AND committed (git)

falsifier.proves_red: RED if: a slate writes with git heads that do not match the live repos; or with a key beyond the read set plus envelope; or beyond the measured ceiling; or a slate file lands in CairnCommons/slates/ that no berth records (a second write path); or migrating this third tenant required a skill_block source change (the template claim, measured a third time).
falsifier.horizon: this session's own close is the door's first live fire — the next slate is written through it or the ticket is not done
